facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old man presented with a 1.5-year history of abdominal pain
three loose, watery stools daily
he had gastroesophageal reflux disease
hereditary hemochromatosis (grade 3 iron overload, mild portal fibrosis, C282Y homozygosity)
he denied rectal bleeding, fever, or weight loss
Vital signs were normal
physical examination was unremarkable
negative ova and parasites, bacterial culture, fecal leukocytes, and Clostridium difficile NAAT
Histoplasma antigen, anti-transglutaminase, and anti-endomysial antibodies were negative
Colonoscopy revealed erythematous mucosa in the transverse colon and rectum and congestion in the terminal ileum
Biopsies from the stomach, duodenum, terminal ileum, colon, and rectum all demonstrated non-caseating microgranulomas
Angiotensin-converting enzyme level was elevated at 77 U/L
A 42-year-old man presented with a 1.5-year history of abdominal pain
three loose, watery stools daily
he had gastroesophageal reflux disease
hereditary hemochromatosis (grade 3 iron overload, mild portal fibrosis, C282Y homozygosity)
he denied rectal bleeding, fever, or weight loss
Vital signs were normal
physical examination was unremarkable
negative ova and parasites, bacterial culture, fecal leukocytes, and Clostridium difficile NAAT
Histoplasma antigen, anti-transglutaminase, and anti-endomysial antibodies were negative
Colonoscopy revealed erythematous mucosa in the transverse colon and rectum and congestion in the terminal ileum
Biopsies from the stomach, duodenum, terminal ileum, colon, and rectum all demonstrated non-caseating microgranulomas
Angiotensin-converting enzyme level was elevated at 77 U/L

concepts.why: Non-caseating microgranulomas and elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level are characteristic of sarcoidosis.
C282Y homozygosity and grade 3 iron overload are diagnostic of hereditary hemochromatosis.
Gastroesophageal reflux disease is suggested by the patient's history of abdominal pain and gastroesophageal reflux disease.
Non-caseating microgranulomas and colonoscopy findings are consistent with Crohn's disease.
Colonoscopy findings and non-caseating microgranulomas could also suggest ulcerative colitis.
Non-caseating microgranulomas and gastrointestinal symptoms could be consistent with Whipple's disease.
Negative anti-transglutaminase and anti-endomysial antibodies make celiac disease less likely, but it cannot be ruled out entirely.
Colonoscopy findings and non-caseating microgranulomas could suggest microscopic colitis.

rationales.F03: Gastroesophageal reflux disease is a common condition, but its presence does not strongly rule in or out other conditions.
rationales.F04: Hereditary hemochromatosis is a specific condition that is strongly suggested by the presence of grade 3 iron overload and C282Y homozygosity.
rationales.F09: Negative tests for celiac disease and Whipple's disease help rule out these conditions.
rationales.F11: Non-caseating microgranulomas are a hallmark of sarcoidosis, but can also be seen in other conditions such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
rationales.F12: Elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level is a specific marker for sarcoidosis.
